change.title: pr-2
change.description: FEATURE: per-topic unsubscribe option in emails
change.author: Régis Hanol

findings.title: Crashes with a 500 when the user has no TopicUser row
findings.body: `TopicUser.find_by` returns nil when the user has never had a topic_users row for this topic. Line 107 then calls `tu.notification_level` on nil and raises NoMethodError. A notification email does not need that row to exist; a mention in a topic the user never opened is one example. So the link in the email can fail with a server error. Fall back to `TopicUser.change(current_user.id, topic_id, notification_level: ...)`, which creates the row when it is missing and also publishes the MessageBus level change, or handle nil explicitly.

findings.title: A GET request changes state, and each visit lowers the level one step
findings.body: The action changes the user's notification level on a plain GET (config/routes.rb:440-441). There is no CSRF token, because `check_xhr` is skipped (line 32). The change also steps down each time: watching/tracking goes to regular, and regular goes to muted. Three problems follow. (1) Any other site can embed `` and silently mute topics for a logged-in visitor. (2) Email link scanners and prefetchers fire the link without the user acting. (3) A user who opens the link twice, or reloads the page, ends up muted, not regular, and nothing tells them. Make the change idempotent: always set one target level (e.g. regular, or muted if already regular, but only through an explicit action). Better, show a confirmation page and apply the change through a POST/PUT.

findings.title: Opening the unsubscribe route inside the app shows the message but changes nothing
findings.body: Only the server action `topics#unsubscribe` changes the notification level. The Ember route's model hook only calls `PostStream.loadTopicView(params.id)`, which loads the topic view and never touches the unsubscribe endpoint. If the user reaches `/t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe` inside the app (an in-app link, or Back/Forward after a cached load), the page still says "You will stop receiving notifications for <title>", but the level is not changed. The user sees a wrong result with no warning. Either call the unsubscribe endpoint from the route (e.g. via `topic.details.updateNotifications`), or word the text so it does not claim a change happened.

findings.title: The message says notifications stop even when the level only dropped to regular
findings.body: When the starting level is watching or tracking, the server sets it to regular (topics_controller.rb:107-108). At regular the user still gets notifications for mentions, quotes and replies. "You will stop receiving notifications" overstates what happened. Consider showing the level that was actually set. The property name `stopNotificiationsText` is also misspelled; the template uses the same spelling.

findings.title: New controller action and toggle logic are untested
findings.body: The only spec change adds `unsubscribe_url` to an existing builder spec. Nothing tests `TopicsController#unsubscribe`: the slug redirect, the watching→regular and regular→muted transitions, or the case with no TopicUser row.

contracts.equivalent_path: TopicUser.change used by the notifications dropdown, which publishes notification_level_change
contracts.before_after: Before: no such endpoint. After: a GET finds the TopicUser row and sets it to regular, or to muted if it was already regular, using tu.save!. Unlike TopicUser.change, it neither creates a missing row nor publishes to MessageBus.
contracts.visible_effect: Renders the show template with the preloaded topic (perform_show_response, line 500). The Ember topicUnsubscribe route then shows the stop_notifications text and the notifications button.
contracts.failure_mode: A nil TopicUser gives NoMethodError (500). A repeated GET mutes the topic. A cross-site GET without CSRF changes state.

contracts.action: Client route topicUnsubscribe loads the topic view
contracts.equivalent_path: topic route, which loads the topic through PostStream.loadTopicView
contracts.before_after: The route only loads the topic and never calls the unsubscribe endpoint.
contracts.visible_effect: Shows the message that notifications stop, whether or not the level changed.
contracts.failure_mode: If loadTopicView rejects, nothing here handles it; the error goes to the default route error handling.
contracts.open_question: Does loadTopicView reuse the server's preloaded data, and what does the route show when loading fails?

contracts.action: Email footer adds a per-topic unsubscribe link
contracts.equivalent_path: user_preferences_url link in the same footer
contracts.before_after: The unsubscribe_link translation now interpolates %{unsubscribe_url}. The only caller with add_unsubscribe_link, user_notifications.rb:294, passes it as an absolute URL (Topic#url uses base_url).
contracts.visible_effect: Notification emails show a 'click here' link to stop notifications for the topic.

summary: The PR adds a per-topic unsubscribe link to notification emails, plus a server endpoint and an Ember page for it. The server action changes state on a GET with no CSRF protection. Each visit lowers the level one more step, so a second click, a reload or a link scanner can mute the topic. It also crashes when the user has no TopicUser row. The client route never calls the endpoint, so navigating there inside the app reports a change that never happened. The email wiring itself is consistent: the only sender with the unsubscribe flag passes an absolute unsubscribe_url.
